title: Community Submission (pending review)
description: Shape of a single file under submissions/pending/. A submission proposes ONE new sustainability_sources entry, either for an existing company (matched by target_company_id) or a brand-new company (target_company_id omitted, new_company filled in instead). Submissions are never written directly into eu_sustainability_sources_v5.json - they sit in submissions/pending/ until a maintainer approves and runs merge_submissions.py. This mirrors a Wikipedia-style 'propose an edit, then a human reviews it' flow rather than direct writes to the live article.

submission_id.description: Unique id for this submission, e.g. 'sub-2026-08-21-0007'. Assigned by validate_submission.py if left blank (see tooling), or by the submitter following the same convention.

submitted_by.description: GitHub username (or name/contact) of the submitter. Required so reviewers can follow up with questions - anonymous submissions are not accepted, same as Wikipedia requiring an attributable account for anything beyond trivial fixes.

target.description: Which company this submission is for. Exactly one of target_company_id (existing company) or new_company (brand-new company) must be set.

target_company_id.description: company_id of an existing company this entry should be added to. Null if this submission is proposing a brand-new company (see new_company).

new_company.description: Set only when target_company_id is null - proposes a company not yet in the dataset.

supersedes_entry_id.description: If this submission should replace an existing entry as the current one (e.g. a newer year's report), set this to that entry's entry_id. On merge, that old entry is automatically flipped to is_legacy:true rather than deleted - history is kept, not overwritten, same as a Wikipedia page history.

entry.description: The proposed sustainability_sources entry itself. Same shape as schema/sustainability_sources.schema.json#/$defs/sourceEntry. NOTE on entry_id: submitters should set it to a placeholder equal to this submission's submission_id (e.g. 'sub-2026-08-21-0007') - that value already satisfies sourceEntry's entry_id pattern, so it validates, but merge_submissions.py OVERWRITES it with a proper '<company_id>-NNN' id (continuing that company's existing sequence) when the submission is merged. Don't hand-pick a '<company_id>-NNN' id yourself; you don't know what NNN should be until merge time.

review.description: Filled in by maintainers, not by the submitter. A submission PR should be opened with this block left at its default ('pending', empty checks) - reviewers fill it in as part of the review, and CI blocks merge_submissions.py from running until status is 'approved'.

checklist.description: Reviewer must be able to check all of these before setting status to 'approved'. See CONTRIBUTING.md for what each check means.
